What the Experts Say This part builds on our price data above. Here is what outside experts say. Underwriters Laboratories (UL) According to UL, Class 4 is the top hail grade a roof can get. The test is called UL 2218. A 2-inch steel ball is dropped on the same spot twice. A Class 4 shingle must not crack. Insurance Institute for Business & Home Safety (IBHS) According to IBHS expert Dr. Ian Giammanco, PhD, managing director of atmospheric science at IBHS, Colorado makes up only about 10% of the national market for impact-resistant shingles, even though the state sits in Hail Alley. IBHS fires lab-made hail at full-size roofs at its research center in South Carolina. In a 2025 study, Giammanco and fellow IBHS researchers found that small hail under 1 inch, which the National Weather Service doesn’t even rate as severe, slowly wears shingles down. Weathered shingles that took small-hail hits were about ten times more likely to be damaged by a later large hailstorm. Impact-resistant shingles held their granules only slightly better under repeated small hail, so every roof should get checked after a hail season, not just after the big storms. It took about eight years of fieldwork to understand all the properties of hail. We replicate that in our laboratory and then we go test the products. — Dr. Ian Giammanco, PhD , managing director of atmospheric science at the Insurance Institute for Business & Home Safety, speaking to KOAA News , December 9, 2025 Rocky Mountain Insurance Association Insurance expert Carole Walker, executive director of the Rocky Mountain Insurance Association, told KOAA News in December 2025 that in Colorado, “many of the insurers give a discount for having hail resistant roofing products.” Ask your insurer what discount applies before you choose a shingle.
